question.problem: What is the value of $x$ given that $a=[\begin{aligned}2x \\ -1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ x\end{aligned}]$ and $a⊥b?$

current_example.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272903/assets/8eae66cd99ec4b0d1551ca2c426fe8b662b2a946da69148fcc38334c22d35ff4.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272903/assets/966ffe2c6d2c11aa4de070ea2675b2376fdc7a23da6298b57407991bf905140e.svg). Given that $\mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b}$, find the value of $t$.
current_example.worked_solution:
We know that $\mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b}$ ($\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are perpendicular) if and only if $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = 0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =4\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot 5+1\cdot t \\  & =-8-10+t \\  & =t-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ t-18 & =0 \\ t & =18\end{aligned}
$$
